clue.text: Metro ride chap arranged to see Parisian landmark

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of these three words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A man shuffles about on the Paris Métro to get to a famous sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges METRO RIDE CHAP, thirteen letters, into the monument's name; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The triumphal arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées is one of the best-known sights in Paris.

clue.text: Book one of the seasonal musical acts

definitions.text: one of the seasonal musical acts
definitions.meaning: a single festive song sung at Yuletide, one item in a programme of such performances

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's festive ghost story shares its title with any single festive song sung in December.

clue.text: Experience trouble with extremely confused topic

indicators.note: something extremely confused is thoroughly mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A muddled subject leads someone into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely confused' signals that TOPIC is rearranged; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is an informal British idiom for getting into trouble or being punished.

clue.text: Tree's fruit found in church office

parts.note: the elder is a tree, here with its possessive S
a hip is the red fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Berries from a tree turn up in a vestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches an elder holds a recognised post, and the position itself is named with the suffix -ship.

clue.text: Artist following the likes of Millais, you might wrongly infer

definitions.text: Artist following the likes of Millais, you might wrongly infer

parts.words: Artist following the likes of Millais, you might wrongly infer
parts.note: Millais belonged to the ...-... Brotherhood; read literally, 'pre' suggests a painter who came after them, but the Italian master lived centuries earlier

explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter whose name the Pre-Raphaelites took is the one they claimed to precede.

clue.text: People swear by them

parts.note: read not as trusting something but as the solemn promises made when giving testimony

explanation.definitionFit: Solemn vows are what a witness swears when promising to tell the truth.

clue.text: I'm appearing with cat in light entertainment for Christmas?

indicators.note: in tells us the cat and the I'm go inside the word for light

parts.note: a pane is a window light, a sheet of glass in a window
a tom is a male cat
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone appears on stage with a cat in a light Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like part of 'light entertainment', but it is the window pane that holds TOM and IM.
explanation.definitionFit: British Christmas tradition includes a comic stage show for families based on a fairy tale, with dames and slapstick.

clue.text: Geezer, once sober, drunk — Christmas spirits transformed him

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old fellow, once teetotal, is now drunk on festive liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GEEZER ONCE SOBER. 'spirits' reads as liquor but means the three ghosts who visit the miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser is reformed by visits from the ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come.

clue.text: Cat — Whittington's first seen with it

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the name

parts.note: being with it means being fashionable or hip

explanation.surface: Dick Whittington's famous cat makes an appearance in the pantomime story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' suggests Whittington's pet, but it is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a lash; 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat-o'-nine-tails was a knotted lash used for flogging, a kind of scourge.

clue.text: Drank excessively on return to regimental HQ

indicators.note: on return says the word for drank too much is read backwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so toped is drank excessively

explanation.surface: A soldier came back to barracks drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's depot is its headquarters and base, where recruits are trained and stores kept.

clue.text: Refrain from Ida, boy

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Refrain from Ida, boy'; the scan's italic word ('Idn'?) is unreadable, so the wordplay for NOEL cannot be confirmed.

clue.text: She helped to introduce Christmas tree here in station

definitions.text: She helped to introduce Christmas tree here
definitions.meaning: the queen whose German husband Albert popularised the decorated fir in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: Many readers credit Prince Albert, but the royal couple together made the custom fashionable in Britain; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian royal household made the decorated fir fashionable, and a London rail terminus shares the queen's name.

clue.text: Provided the necessary material for a seasonal ball

definitions.text: Provided the necessary material for a seasonal ball

parts.words: Provided the necessary material for a seasonal ball
parts.note: reads like supplying a winter dance, but describes the weather that lets children make a ball to throw

explanation.definitionFit: A fall of flakes supplies exactly what is needed to pack a winter missile.

clue.text: Uncle's protector who drops in on Christmas Eve

definitions.meaning: 'uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, and this saint is their patron

definitions.text: who drops in on Christmas Eve
definitions.meaning: the saint behind Santa Claus, who comes down chimneys

explanation.definitionFit: The bishop of Myra is patron saint of pawnbrokers and the original of Father Christmas.

clue.text: Popular and lively type having a ball

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a swinger is a lively, fun-loving person

explanation.surface: A popular, lively person is out enjoying themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a ball' suggests a good time, but 'ball' is the definition, a cricket delivery; 'having a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a delivery that curves in the air towards the batsman is a type of bowled ball.

clue.text: Evil group corrupted assistant

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A villainous gang led a helper astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil worshippers form a sinister band, a fair picture of wickedness collectively.

clue.text: Holly helping to make domicile Xmassy

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is part of the following words, which help form it

explanation.surface: Sprigs of holly give a house a festive look.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'domicile' into the start of 'Xmassy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus name for the hollies.

clue.text: Congregate for service

definitions.meaning: to gather together in a crowd
the Eucharist as a church service

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to gather in a crowd; as a noun it is the Catholic Eucharist service.

clue.text: Employ this organisation believing in diversity?

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A company recruits staff for its diversity policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like a company but signals rearranging EMPLOY THIS. The definition is playful: diversity of gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of many gods is belief in a variety of deities, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Scholar in a form of Islam converted to Eastern religion

indicators.note: in tells us the scholar sits inside the rearranged faith
a form of says the word is reshaped into a different arrangement

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

explanation.surface: An academic in a version of Islam converts to a faith from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a form of' rearranges ISLAM to LAISM, which takes MA; 'converted to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibetan Buddhism, headed by the Dalai Lama, is a faith of Asia.

clue.text: Chinese work hard in decoration of Christmas cake

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for hard goes inside the cake topping

parts.note: icing covers and decorates a British Christmas cake
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone toils at decorating the Christmas cake with Chinese designs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Changes is an ancient Chinese divination text.

clue.text: Relish being in the ring after sudden blow?

indicators.note: after puts the ring at the end, following the blow

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A boxer revels in the ring after landing a sudden punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' suggests a boxer's punch, but it is a blast of wind; 'being in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiasm and zest are what 'relish' means as a noun here.

clue.text: Government department making some cars do test

parts.note: Minis are a classic British make of small car
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A ministry arranges for a few cars to undergo testing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministry is a major branch of state administration headed by a minister.

clue.text: High-class supporters turned up in utter confusion

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: U stands for upper-class
fans are supporters

explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses U plus FANS, UFANS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A military slang acronym for a chaotic mess, a botched situation.

clue.text: Prison ship

definitions.meaning: a military or naval lock-up, especially in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a naval guardhouse and a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Going by air, three early Christmas Day arrivals I spotted

definitions.text: Going by air, three early Christmas Day arrivals I spotted

parts.words: Going by air, three early Christmas Day arrivals I spotted
parts.note: 'air' is a tune, not flight: the carol 'I saw three ... come sailing in on Christmas Day in the morning'

explanation.definitionFit: The carol says three vessels came sailing in on Christmas morning.

clue.text: Star travelling from the East to area in West

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A star journeys from the East, like the Magi's, toward western lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling from the East' reverses NOVA; 'to' is a link. AVON was a county in the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Avon was a former county around Bristol in the West Country of England.

clue.text: Peer in bad government who's leading Christmas revels?

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
of can mean in, as in 'a man of the people'
misrule is bad government

explanation.surface: A nobleman in a corrupt administration heads the festive partying.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval and Tudor England an appointed master of ceremonies presided over festive merrymaking.
